target.title: feat(mac): show native notification permission in dashboard Notifications settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI Settings → Notifications page only knows about browser web push. Inside the macOS app's embedded dashboard (WKWebView), web push is unsupported, so the page shows "Unsupported / Not subscribed" even though the Mac app delivers notifications natively through `UNUserNotificationCenter` (the node runtime's notify path). Users see a dead, misleading settings page in the app that actually has the best notification support.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard webview is "only partially a website": the host app owns notification delivery, so the page must reflect the host's native permission state instead of browser push capability. This adds a small WebKit script-message bridge (`openclawNotifications`) following the existing dashboard bridge patterns (`openclawLink`, `openclawWindowDrag`, `openclawUpdate`):

- The Mac app registers the handler on the dashboard webview and answers `status` / `request-permission` / `send-test` requests, publishing `{permission: granted|denied|notDetermined}` back via the same CustomEvent+global pattern as the native history bridge. `request-permission` reuses `PermissionManager.ensure([.notifications], interactive: true)`, which prompts when undetermined and opens System Settings → Notifications when denied. `send-test` posts a real native notification.
- The Control UI probes the handler; when present, the Notifications settings section renders native state (permission chip, Enable / Open System Settings / Send test) instead of the web-push rows. Browsers keep the existing web-push UI unchanged. Permission changes made in System Settings are picked up on window focus.
- The notifications section renderer moved out of the grandfathered oversized `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` into `ui/src/pages/config/notifications-section.ts`.

## User Impact

Mac app users see real notification state on Settings → Notifications: whether the app can notify, a one-click permission request, a shortcut to System Settings when denied, and a native test notification. No behavior change for browsers or other hosts (handler absent → web-push UI as before).

## Evidence

- `cd apps/macos && swift build` — Build complete (verified twice, including after the `.ephemeral` cleanup below).
- `cd apps/macos && swift test --filter DashboardNotificationsBridgeTests` — 3 tests pass (request parsing, invalid-request rejection, permission-label mapping including raw-value-4 ephemeral → notDetermined).
- New UI unit tests in `ui/src/app/native-notifications.test.ts` cover bridge probe, status seeding from the injected global, event validation, focus re-sync, action posting, and dispose; they run in the UI CI lane (this worktree has no node_modules, so UI test execution is delegated to hosted CI per repo policy).
- `git diff --check` clean; changed TS files formatted with oxfmt.
- Structured autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`): one P1 raised on an earlier revision (`UNAuthorizationStatus.ephemeral` is unavailable-by-name on macOS; it compiled only because pattern position tolerates it). Resolved by dropping the case into a commented `default` branch; the rerun reports "patch is correct" with zero findings.
- `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` (grandfathered oversized) shrank by ~150 lines via the section extraction; web-push rendering is byte-identical to before.
- Trust guards on the new bridge mirror `receiveUpdateMessage`: main frame only, same webview, `isTrustedLinkSource` origin/path check.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.37.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.37.1

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

target.title: fix(sandbox): make stat output locale independent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106576.

Sandbox `stat` previously treated missing files by searching `stderr` for the English text `No such file or directory`. That made normal `stat()` calls throw instead of returning `null` when the sandbox shell localized native error output.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the `stat` contract away from localized shell text:

- the anchored sandbox stat script now emits a fixed `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` sentinel before invoking `stat` when the basename is absent
- successful stat output now uses GNU stat raw mode bits (`%f`) plus numeric size/mtime fields instead of localized `%F` file-type names and `%y` date text
- the remote fs bridge now parses the same raw mode bits for stat and hardlink checks, keeping the sibling shell-backed path aligned

Non-missing stat failures still throw, so permission/tool/runtime errors do not get collapsed into a false missing-file result.

## User Impact

Localized sandbox/container environments can now call sandbox `stat()` on absent paths without crashing the file bridge. File, directory, size, mtime, and hardlink behavior stays deterministic without depending on the host shell language.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.anchored-ops.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts`
- Docker image pull was unavailable in the intranet Linux environment, so runtime proof used the exact POSIX shell/stat contract that the sandbox bridge now emits, on Linux with localized `LANG=de_DE.UTF-8`:
  - missing path prints `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` and exits 0
  - normal file/dir `stat -c "%f|%s|%Y"` returns raw mode, size, epoch seconds
  - genuine non-missing stat failure preserves nonzero exit and stderr

target.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap
target.body:
Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` fallback), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey`), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. The Codex review classified this as P0 / impact:security with 0.96 confidence.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MEMORY.md should not be injected as a bootstrap file in shared channel (group/channel) sessions
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/group-session-memory-privacy-108881`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/workspace.test.ts src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts src/routing/session-key.test.ts --run
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. All 9 shared channel session key types (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal + thread/legacy variants) exclude MEMORY.md from bootstrap
  2. All 5 private session key types (main, chat, direct, DM) retain MEMORY.md
  3. Hook-injected MEMORY.md is re-stripped by `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` for group sessions
  4. Hook-injected lowercase `memory.md` alias is also stripped for group sessions
  5. Subagent and cron allowlists unchanged
-  Sending a real message to a live Telegram group / Discord guild and observing the agent's response not contain private memory content. This requires running gateway + channel bot credentials which are not available in CI. The **live chain verification above** and the **canary integration tests below** prove the complete code path from `buildAgentPeerSessionKey` through `isSharedChannelSessionKey` through `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` through `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` — every production function in the critical path is exercised with real inputs and outputs.

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. 2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) and attaches `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never removed on `close`. On the success path the resolved stream kept its `data` listeners attached, so the resolved stream object could be retained after the promise settles.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR originally also added `child.unref()` to let a completed run not keep the caller alive. ClawSweeper review correctly noted (P2) that `child.unref()` alone is **ineffective** here: `runQaCli` still waits for `close` while retaining its piped `stdout`/`stderr` and its timeout handle, so unref-ing only the child-process handle does not let the parent exit sooner — and a real subprocess reproduction was not available to justify the lifecycle mutation. A detached child that the parent must read to completion is *supposed* to keep the event loop alive until `close`; unref-ing it would risk the parent exiting before reading the output.

So this revision **drops the ineffective `child.unref()`** (and the test that asserted it) and keeps only the legitimate, observable improvement: detaching both `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners in the `close` handler so the resolved stream is not retained.

## User Impact

- No behavior change to when `runQaCli` resolves (still waits for `close`).
- Success path no longer retains `data` listeners on the resolved streams (cleaner teardown).

## Evidence

- Regression test "detaches stdout/stderr data listeners on close so the resolved stream is not retained": asserts stdio `data` listeners are detached on `close`. Green after the fix; the `unref` assertion was removed because `unref()` is no longer called.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` attached `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never detached on `close`, so the resolved stream could be retained after the promise settled. The fix removes both listeners in the `close` handler. The originally proposed `child.unref()` was removed: a detached child the parent reads to completion is intended to hold the event loop until `close`, and `unref()` alone does not change that while the piped stdio and timeout handles remain referenced (confirmed by source inspection + ClawSweeper review; no real subprocess reproduction was available to justify it).

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed listener-detach path is driven through a mocked `node:child_process`.

Evidence after fix (mocked child_process suite):
- "detaches stdout/stderr data listeners on close so the resolved stream is not retained" -> listeners detached on `close`
- "runs the qa cli through the resolved node executable" -> resolves with collected output

Observed result after fix: the detached child is read to completion and both stream listeners are detached on `close`; the ineffective `unref()` mutation is removed so no unproven lifecycle claim remains.

What was not tested: A real subprocess spawn against a live qa-cli binary was not executed (the spawn is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — listener cleanup on `close`. A real subprocess reproduction to justify a future `unref()`/timeout change is noted as follow-up but is not claimed as done.

target.title: fix(gateway): worker workspaces recover after stalled process probes
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cloud worker workspace sessions could remain quiesced
indefinitely when the detached expiry watchdog's process identity probe stalled
and did not exit after `SIGTERM`. Because the parent SSH command had already
returned, no outer command deadline remained to release the lease.

## Why This Change Was Made

The detached watchdog now runs its `ps` identity probe asynchronously with a
one-second deadline. When that deadline expires, it closes the probe pipes,
force-terminates and unreferences the child, and retries the full lease check
without waiting for the probe to exit. PID start-time matching remains required
before `SIGCONT`, so recovery does not weaken process identity safety.

## User Impact

Expired cloud worker workspace leases can recover even when a host process probe
ignores normal termination. Identity-matched frozen processes resume and the
lease is removed instead of leaving the workspace unavailable indefinitely.
There are no config, schema, protocol, or migration changes.

## Evidence

- Node.js 24 documents that `execFileSync()` still waits for a timed-out child
  that handles or ignores `SIGTERM`, confirming why the prior synchronous
  timeout could not enforce the watchdog deadline.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-sync-scripts.test.ts`
  - 1 test file passed
  - 9 tests passed
  - Includes a regression whose first `ps` process records its PID, ignores
    `SIGTERM`, and sleeps; the watchdog must retry and release the lease.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...`, targeted `oxlint`, and
  `git diff --check` passed for both changed files.
- Near-real owner-runtime proof executed the production generated quiescence
  script with a real detached watchdog, real lease persistence, and a real
  POSIX target process:
  - heartbeat bytes before/while stopped: `3 -> 3`
  - first identity probe ignored `SIGTERM`
  - lease removed and target resumed in 3.778 seconds
  - heartbeat bytes after release: `4`

### Proof boundary

The runtime proof uses real processes and `SIGSTOP`/`SIGCONT` on a local Linux
host. Only `ps` is replaced to inject one deterministic signal-resistant stall.
This is not a hosted cloud-worker run, so provider-host-specific process behavior
remains an external proof gap.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. A 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. When a file exceeds the cap the scanner cannot know which exclusions the user asked for, so it fails closed: it conservatively excludes that directory's whole subtree from the scan. The exclusion is terminal for the directory — processing stops there so a later ignore file cannot negate it and reopen a subtree whose policy could not be parsed. Symlinked ignore files are still followed to their final regular target, preserving legacy workspace behavior.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- An oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` now hides its subtree from discovery (fail closed) instead of dropping all of its exclusions (fail open). Workspaces with ignore files over 4 MiB will see that subtree disappear from scans until the file is trimmed below the cap.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with a bounded `readRegularFileSync({ maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` read in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, after a direct size check that signals oversize.
- On oversize, the matcher adds `<prefix>**` and the per-directory ignore-file loop stops, so no later file can re-include the excluded subtree.
- `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covers normal files, under-cap large files, oversized files, cross-file negation (oversized `.gitignore` + later `!pattern` in `.ignore`, and oversized `.fdignore` + earlier negation), and symlink chains.
- Local test run on the final head:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 6 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof (standalone, final head 01d3b33e2)

Standalone script driving the real `addIgnoreRules` / `loadSkillsFromDir` scan path in temp workspaces (no test-runner mocks):

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js: true
  ignores src/main.ts: false
=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.6 MB) ===
  file size: 2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB): fail-closed subtree exclusion ===
  file size: 13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
  ignores anything/else.txt: true
=== Oversized .gitignore + later negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite later negation: true
  ignores secret.txt despite later negation: true
=== Oversized .fdignore + negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite earlier negation: true
=== Skill discovery: oversized .gitignore + negating .ignore hides the skill ===
  skills discovered: 0
=== Symlinked .gitignore still honored ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

- A 2.6 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file now excludes its whole subtree (fail closed), and later `!` negations in other ignore files of the same directory cannot reopen it.
- A skill directory hidden by an oversized policy is not discovered even when a later ignore file explicitly negates it.
- Symlinked `.gitignore` files are resolved to their final regular target and honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

target.title: fix(commands): distinguish user No from Cancel in confirm prompts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user answers No to Proceed with reset? or Proceed with uninstall? in `src/commands/reset.ts:119` and `src/commands/uninstall.ts:173`, the condition `isCancel(ok) || !ok` treats it identically to Ctrl+C cancel, showing Reset cancelled. / Uninstall cancelled. This is misleading the user didnt cancel they explicitly declined.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bug is in the condition itself: isCancel checks for Ctrl+C/Escape (the @clack/prompts cancel symbol), while !ok catches the user clicking No. These are semantically distinct user intents and should produce different messages.

## User Impact

- Before: Answering No shows Reset cancelled. / Uninstall cancelled. despite not being a cancellation
- After: No shows Reset skipped. / Uninstall skipped.; only Ctrl+C/Escape shows cancelled
- Functionally identical: both paths exit(0)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** User No conflated with Cancel in both reset and uninstall confirm prompts
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24, commit `5ea73a1e6` on branch `fix/confirm-no-vs-cancel` (rebased on upstream/main `94e1cc9a4`)
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts` with a test file that mocks `@clack/prompts.confirm` to return `false` (No) and `Symbol.for("clack:cancel")` (Ctrl+C), then calls BOTH real `resetCommand()` AND real `uninstallCommand()` with a mock runtime. Verifies output messages and exit codes for both commands.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node`/`vitest` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  stdout | resetCommand: shows skipped when user answers No
  reset No: log=["Reset skipped."]

  stdout | resetCommand: shows cancelled when user presses Ctrl+C
  [CANCEL]: Reset cancelled.
  reset Cancel: log=[]

  stdout | uninstallCommand: shows skipped when user answers No
  uninstall No: log=["Uninstall skipped."]

  stdout | uninstallCommand: shows cancelled when user presses Ctrl+C
  [CANCEL]: Uninstall cancelled.
  uninstall Cancel: log=[]

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real `resetCommand` invocation: No shows "Reset skipped.", Ctrl+C shows "[CANCEL]: Reset cancelled.". Real `uninstallCommand` invocation: No shows "Uninstall skipped.", Ctrl+C shows "[CANCEL]: Uninstall cancelled.". Both paths exit(0) correctly for both commands.
- **What was not tested:** Live CLI prompt interaction (CI will cover via existing command tests)

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test src/commands/reset.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       3 passed (3)
```

Existing command tests pass. Real `resetCommand` AND `uninstallCommand` runtime verified via vitest with mocked @clack/prompts across 4 scenarios (2 commands x 2 confirm responses).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes message changes from cancelled to skipped when user answers No
- Config/env/migration behavior: No
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No
- Highest-risk area: Message string change
- Mitigation: Both paths exit(0) identically; only the display message changes; real runtime verified for both reset and uninstall

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(usage-bar): clear dead watcher reference after transient error
target.body:
## Summary
Clear both `entry.watcher` and `entry.template` when a usage bar template file watcher hits a transient error, so the next access re-reads from disk and creates a fresh watcher — whether the template was valid or invalid at the time of the error.

## What Problem This Solves
After a usage bar template file watcher (`src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.ts`) hits a transient filesystem error, the error handler called `watcher.close()` but left the cache entry intact. `loadUsageBarTemplate` at line 184 checks `cached.template ?? (cached.watcher ? undefined : cacheTemplateFile(path))` — a truthy cached template short-circuits the re-read, so edits after the watcher error are never observed.

The original fix (PR head `2da5c8f`) cleared only `entry.watcher`. This recovered the case where the template was already `undefined` (invalidated by a prior change event before the error), but left the common case unaddressed: a valid cached template that stays stale indefinitely after its watcher dies.

**Code evidence**: [template.ts:157-160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.ts#L157-L160)

## Root Cause
- Bug present since the watcher was added in [#98990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98990)
- Invariant violated: a closed FSWatcher must not be treated as "still watching." The cache logic at line 184 uses truthiness of both `entry.template` and `entry.watcher` — both must be cleared for recovery.
- Trigger: any transient inotify/kqueue watcher error, regardless of the template's current cached state.

## Why This Fix
Clear `entry.template = undefined` alongside `entry.watcher = undefined`. This makes the cache entry eligible for full re-read on the next access:
- **Valid template case**: File was valid → watcher errors → file is edited → next load re-reads → picks up the edit
- **Invalid template case** (already covered): File was invalidated → watcher errors → next load re-reads → picks up new content

This matches the recovery pattern from [#109682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109682) (config hot-reload watcher recovery, 🦞).

## User Impact
- **Before**: After a transient watcher error, users see stale usage bar footer content indefinitely. Only cache eviction (64 other paths loaded) or gateway restart recovers.
- **After**: The next `loadUsageBarTemplate` call re-reads from disk and creates a fresh watcher. Template edits are picked up within one access.

## Evidence
- **Before**: Watcher error → stale template served forever
- **After**: Watcher error → `entry.template = undefined` + `entry.watcher = undefined` → next load re-reads from disk
- Two regression tests: invalid-template recovery AND valid-template recovery after watcher error

## Real Behavior Proof

### Valid-template recovery after watcher error (new test)

```bash
$ node --require ./scripts/proof-watcher-patch.cjs --import tsx scripts/proof-usage-bar-watcher-error.mjs
Step 1: Load valid template
  PASS: valid template loaded
  watchers captured: 1
Step 2: Inject transient watcher error (template still valid)
  error emitted on captured watcher
Step 3: Write new content and reload
  PASS: template recovery after watcher error  ← new: valid-cache path
  Template: {"segments":[{"text":"CUSTOM-B-RECOVERED"}]}
VERDICT: PASS — template recovers after watcher error
```

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.test.ts
 ✓ 15/15 passed
     ✓ recovers after watcher error by clearing the dead watcher reference
     ✓ reloads a still-valid template after watcher error
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.watcher-proof.test.ts
 ✓ 1/1 passed (0 watchers leaked)
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.test.ts` — 15/15 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/template.watcher-proof.test.ts` — 1/1 passed (0 leaked)
- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (extracted to `packages/media-core`) that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
  - Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop before decode
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Codex OAuth image result route guard (ClawSweeper P1)

The reviewer flagged that the documented Codex OAuth Responses route (`extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`) returned a base64 `b64_json` image result and needed the configured byte budget applied before decode. At the current head this is guarded end to end. Source trace of the exact-head control flow:

- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1044` — `const maxImageBytes = resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(req.cfg)` (resolved from `cfg.agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, else `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`).
- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1049-1059` — the response is parsed with `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse(data, { ..., maxBytes: maxImageBytes })`. **This `maxBytes` argument is new vs `upstream/main`** (main's call site does not pass `maxBytes`).
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:221` — `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` accepts `maxBytes` and forwards it to `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:199-219` — forwards `maxBytes` to `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:150-155` — `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes(base64)` and returns `undefined` (drops the entry, no `Buffer.from` decode) when `estimatedSize > params.maxBytes`.

So an oversized Codex OAuth `b64_json` result is dropped **before** base64 decode, with no allocation of the decoded buffer. The guard is applied on the exact OAuth result path the reviewer named.

Exact-head runtime output (synthetic controlled payloads via in-repo boundary tests):
```
# src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts (added this head)
- "drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)"
    -> 2-entry response: small (accepted) + 200-char base64 over 10-byte cap (dropped)
    -> images.length === 1, images[0].buffer === "tiny"
```

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: boundary tests in `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB
  - Codex OAuth route: oversized `b64_json` entry dropped before decode when `maxBytes` set

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Oversized base64-encoded images could be decoded before any size check, causing transient memory exhaustion (defense-in-depth DoS). The fix estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` and rejects over-limit input **before** decoding in `writeCliImages` (CLI staging), `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` (provider image parsing), and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`), propagating the existing `maxBytes`/`generatedMediaMaxBytes` limit.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The guard is exercised by the in-repo boundary tests that feed controlled base64 payloads (7MB / 8MB / 10MB) and assert accept/reject decisions before decode, plus the new route-level test for the Codex OAuth path.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
 - rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
 - accepts 7MB payload under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
 - rejects 10MB payload under 8MB limit
 - rejects 7MB payload under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
 - drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)
```

Observed result after fix: Payloads exceeding the configured/default media size limit are rejected before any `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` decode, so oversized input cannot trigger transient memory pressure. Configured limits above the default are honored. The Codex OAuth image-generation result route now applies the same `maxBytes` budget before decoding. No new configuration surface was added (uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes`).

What was not tested: Live provider out-of-memory reproduction was not run (neither necessary nor safely desirable — the reviewer agreed); the proof targets the exact changed guard branches with synthetic over-limit payloads.

target.title: fix(reef): repeated relay reconnects no longer leave stale sockets active
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a local Reef frame-processing failure could allow a replacement WebSocket generation to start while the abandoned socket was still closing. Repeated failures could therefore overlap stale and replacement sockets and leave stale socket activity during channel shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Reef inbox WebSocket generation now owns one bounded terminal transition. A locally failed generation preserves its original error, waits for its close handshake before allowing reconnect, and force-terminates after five seconds if the peer does not finish closing. The implementation is rebased onto the current durable-cursor and serialized-recovery lifecycle from `main`, which already removes each generation's abort listener on terminal transition; the regression coverage preserves that existing invariant.

## User Impact

Long-running Reef channels can reconnect repeatedly without overlapping failed and replacement sockets. Channel abort closes the active generation and waits for both its socket and in-flight serialized work to finish.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto pinned current `main` (`5057fd9e597`) and resolved the two conflicting Reef transport files against the newer durable recovery implementation.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts`
  - 1 test file passed
  - 27 tests passed
  - Covers the current durable recovery suite plus the existing active-generation listener invariant, malformed-frame error preservation, close-before-reconnect ordering, and forced termination of a stalled close.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/reef/src/transport.ts extensions/reef/src/transport.test.ts`
  - All matched files use the correct format.
- `node scripts/check-max-lines-ratchet.mjs --base 5057fd9e597`
  - Passed with 1,169 grandfathered suppressions and no new max-lines regression.
- Near-real network proof used the production `createReefWebSocket` client against a local protocol-compatible WebSocket relay. Redacted event order:

```text
connected:1
sent:malformed-frame
state:connected
state:disconnected
closed:1
error:original-malformed-frame
connected:2
replacement-after-close
state:connected
abort:channel
state:disconnected
closed:2
```

  Assertions passed: two generations observed; failed generation closed before replacement; original malformed-frame failure preserved; final abort closed the replacement; zero relay peers remained.

### Proof boundary

The live proof uses real `ws` network sockets and the production Reef transport owner, with a local protocol-compatible relay rather than a hosted Reef service. A full gateway startup is not the canonical owner of this ordering: malformed-frame handling, socket close completion, reconnect, and abort cleanup all occur inside `ReefInboxConnection`.

target.title: feat(macos): Quick Chat area capture and focused-app text context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS Quick Chat could attach a whole window screenshot but nothing more precise, and it had no way to hand the agent the text you're actually looking at. Region capture is table stakes across quick bars; focused-app text context is cheaper, sharper, and more actionable than pixels.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Drag-select region capture**: the camera button becomes a native two-item menu (Capture Window… / Capture Area…). The area flow raises per-screen overlay panels with crosshair drag, outside-dim, a live size badge, and Esc/tiny-drag cancel; on mouse-up the overlays tear down first (matching the window picker's settle), the bar is hidden synchronously (a fast drag must never capture a fading composer), and the selection converts from AppKit bottom-left space to the top-left global display coordinates Peekaboo's `captureArea` expects (conversion verified against the pinned Peekaboo 3.9.3 source, ScreenCaptureKit and legacy paths). The image rides the existing capture pipeline (ownership tokens, off-main processing, same attachment path).
- **Focused-app text context**: a doc-text button captures the frontmost app's focused-window text via a bounded Accessibility walk (the bar is a nonactivating panel, so the user's app stays frontmost). Bounds are real, not aspirational: depth/element/char caps, ancestry-scoped echo suppression that preserves repeated sibling content, per-element AX messaging timeouts, cooperative cancellation, and a hard outer race that abandons a hung walk (structured groups join cancelled children — the race is deliberately unstructured, commented). The result is a removable context chip; on send the text is appended as a labeled context block, and the chip clears on send and on hide so stale context can't leak. Accessibility-only permission, user-initiated prompt, no AX content logged or persisted.

## User Impact

Capture exactly the region you mean, or hand the agent the text of the app you're working in, straight from the bar. Docs updated (`docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md`).

## Evidence

- `swift build` (release) green; SwiftFormat/SwiftLint clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- New tests: region normalization (corner-agnostic drags, tiny-drag cancel, multi-display conversion), collector bounding (depth/element/char caps, truncation marker, sibling preservation, cancellation, expired deadline), chip lifecycle, message assembly.
- Structured second-model review over five rounds: blur-race, dedup-semantics, timeout-coverage, structured-join, and fade-race findings all fixed with regression coverage; final round clean ("patch is correct").
- Live interaction screenshots follow in a PR comment during the CI window.

target.title: feat(memory): default cross-conversation recall for personal installs
target.body:
Related: #99611
Follow-up to #100140.

## What Problem This Solves

Personal-agent installs currently require an explicit opt-in before Active Memory can recall relevant context across conversation boundaries. This compatibility-sensitive default-flip follow-up makes that personal-install behavior available by default while preserving isolation for multi-user-shaped configurations.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single resolver now applies the approved gate: an explicit `rememberAcrossConversations` value always wins; otherwise the setting is on only when global `session.dmScope` is unset or `main` and no route binding has a `session.dmScope` override. Recall is per-agent/private-shaped rather than per-sender, so any configured DM isolation signals a multi-user install where silent cross-sender recall would be a leak.

All core, memory-host, Active Memory, QMD-export, and doctor consumers use the resolved value. Help and memory/recall docs describe the same conditional default.

## User Impact

Personal installs receive cross-conversation recall by default. Configurations with global or per-binding DM isolation remain default-off. Explicit true or false remains authoritative.

This is user-visible behavior and should be called out in release notes as the compatibility-sensitive default change following #100140 / #99611. `CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally unchanged in this contributor branch.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes issues where users piping auth or config input could make the CLI buffer an unbounded stream, and where slow-drip provider or NAS response bodies could keep operations alive beyond their wall-clock budgets.

The same review also found duplicated provider polling/error-body logic and an unreachable OpenAI tool-schema compatibility branch that made these timing and schema invariants harder to maintain.

## Why This Change Was Made

This consolidates the five reviewed drafts into one bounded-I/O design:

- one byte-stream limit helper owns piped stdin caps and safe stream teardown;
- one response-body reader accepts the remaining operation budget lazily, so polling JSON, error details, and generated-media downloads cannot reset a wall-clock deadline per chunk;
- provider-specific retry and timeout behavior stays local while shared polling and body-read mechanics are centralized;

The deterministic native SSE outer-abort regression from #109185 is already present on current main and remains green on this head, so it is not duplicated here.

target.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold
target.body:
Closes #106231

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and reviewed this change under contributor direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent that reached the critical tool-loop threshold would only emit a warning and continue running. The run could keep consuming tokens or repeating tool side effects until a separate timeout or limit stopped it, including through the embedded, Codex, and Copilot harness paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed critical-loop signal now flows from the detector through each harness to one run-terminal owner. That owner stops the active attempt, preserves an earlier user or plugin cancellation, returns the normal blocked-run result, and leaves the session available for the next user turn. Codex native-hook outcomes are also relayed back to loop detection, while duplicate native/managed observations are idempotent.

## User Impact

Critical tool loops now stop the current run at the configured critical threshold instead of continuing indefinitely. Existing warning thresholds, ordinary tool failures and retries, explicit cancellation precedence, and subsequent use of the same session remain intact.

## Evidence

- Added focused coverage for threshold signaling, outcome ordering, duplicate native/managed observations, cancellation races, persistence, session adoption, usage/replay bookkeeping, Codex managed/native hooks, `/btw`, and the Copilot bridge.
- Two independent source audits found no actionable defects after the cancellation, native-hook, side-question, and deduplication edge cases were addressed.
- Fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted`: no accepted/actionable findings (`overall_correctness: patch is correct`, confidence `0.87`).
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes. A clean rebase onto current `upstream/main` preserved the stable patch ID, and the intervening upstream commits did not touch the changed files.
- Dependency contract checked against `openai/codex@2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3`: [`success: false` dynamic-tool responses remain normal tool outputs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), and native [pre/post hooks share the tool call identity and response lifecycle](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs).

## What Problem This Solves

`sliceMarkdownIR` uses `String.prototype.slice()` on code-unit positions to slice IR text. When the slice boundary falls in the middle of a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK supplementary character), the resulting text contains orphaned surrogates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce invalid Unicode strings downstream, potentially corrupting rendered markdown or downstream consumers.

## User Impact

Markdown rendering of messages containing emoji or CJK characters near chunk boundaries may produce broken replacement glyphs.

## Evidence

All 34 existing tests pass plus the new surrogate pair safety test.

target.title: improve(ui): settings cleanup batch — universal config.changed emitter, synced chat prefs, dedupe and copy fixes
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

Follow-up cleanup batch from a fresh audit of the settings restructure (#110445, #110494). It closes the remaining behavior gap and removes drift the redesign left behind:

- **`config.changed` was only broadcast for gateway RPC writes.** Agent `config_set`, CLI, and doctor writes land through the config file watcher's reload path, which never notified connected UIs — so a synced pref changed by the agent didn't propagate live. The event now has a single emitter in the reload committer (`onConfigCandidateCommitted`), covering every accepted write including runtime-skipped ones (writer-intent echo suppression, reload mode `off`). The duplicate RPC-side broadcasts are deleted.
- **Two chat prefs didn't sync across devices.** `chatPersistCommentary` and `chatFollowUpMode` were browser-local; they are now part of the `ui.prefs` sync surface (schema + types + docs), with `chatFollowUpMode` supporting clearable reset (JSON merge-patch `null` removal). `server-prefs.ts` is rewritten around a descriptor table so adding a synced pref is one entry instead of five hand-written code sites.
- **Users couldn't tell which settings roam.** Synced rows/sections now carry a "Synced across your devices through the gateway." caption (chat prefs, theme, language).
- **Duplicated constants.** Security page's tool-profile list and General's thinking levels now derive from the canonical `PROFILE_OPTIONS` / `BASE_THINKING_LEVELS` sources instead of parallel literals.
- **Dead code/copy from the restructure.** Removed the unused `mode: "model"` branch from the composer model controls, the orphaned `.config-view-toggle` CSS family, the stale "Edit openclaw.json." settings subtitle, "Simple view"/"quick-settings card" doc wording, and a stale e2e describe title.
- **Search coverage.** Sessions and Managed Worktrees pages (no schema-backed section) now have static settings-search entries.
- **Stale docs.** `docs/cli/openclaw.md`'s config-write policy paragraph predated the narrowed system-agent denylist; it now documents the actual policy (denylist roots, route-backing plugin guard, per-agent routing escalations).

Deliberately skipped: renaming the `quickSettings.*` i18n namespace to match the new page names. It would force retranslation of every key across all locales for zero user-visible change; a comment at the namespace now records that decision.

# Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-requested audit sweep ("check everything again… do all of that, PR, land") after landing the settings restructure. The `config.changed` gap was a real P1 for the new cross-device pref sync; the rest keeps the redesign from fossilizing drift.

# User Impact

- Prefs changed by the agent (or CLI/doctor) now update open Control UIs live instead of after a reload.
- Chat follow-up mode and commentary persistence follow you across devices.
- Settings UI labels which preferences are synced; settings search finds the Sessions/Worktrees pages.
- No config-shape breaks: `ui.prefs` additions are optional keys; removed surfaces were dead code.

# Evidence

- `src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts` (136 tests): new coverage for notify-on-runtime-skipped edits and reload-mode-off, echo suppression asserted.
- `ui/src/app/server-prefs.test.ts`: descriptor-table sync incl. clearable `null` reset round-trip.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`: new provenance-row test (inherited muted state, override reset commits `""`).
- `ui/src/pages/config/settings-search.test.ts`: worktrees static-entry routing.
- Focused suites for config quick/security/app-navigation/identity-section green; tsgo ui+core lanes; oxlint clean; i18n baseline/verify clean.

target.title: fix(vydra): apply request policy to shared provider HTTP config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Vydra shared provider's `resolveVydraRequestContext()` was not forwarding user-configured provider request policies (timeouts, retries, proxy settings) through `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest`. User-configured request policies were silently ignored for Vydra providers. Other providers (openrouter #104835, xai #104836) already apply this standard policy pattern.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Vydra shared config now imports `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest` and passes the user-configured `request` parameter to `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig()`. All other provider logic, default request behavior, and non-HTTP transport paths are unchanged. The change follows the exact same pattern already merged and proven for openrouter (#104835) and xai (#104836).

## User Impact

Users configuring custom request policies for Vydra providers (e.g., extended timeouts for video generation) now have those settings honored instead of silently ignored, matching the behavior of all other providers.

## Evidence

- **Pattern consistency**: The `request:` parameter is now passed identically to openrouter (#104835) and xai (#104836) ??same import, same `sanitizeConfiguredModelProviderRequest` call, same position in the config object.

target.title: fix(cron): tighten cron tool JSON schema to reduce grammar complexity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with the cron tool: (1) overly permissive JSON schema (`additionalProperties: true`) allowed grammatically complex expressions that increased grammar parsing complexity and risked parse failures, and (2) agent-turn cron jobs could bypass creator tool allowlists because tool allowlist capping was missing for agent-turn payloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

All 7 schema definitions in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` now use `additionalProperties: false` to reduce the grammar state space and catch invalid inputs at schema validation time. New `capCronAgentTurnToolsAllow()` family of functions enforces creator tool allowlists on agent-turn cron payloads (create, update, and patch paths), handling wildcard `"*"`, plugin groups, and default markers. Valid cron expressions and non-agent-turn functionality are unchanged.

## User Impact

Cron expressions that previously risked grammar parse failures due to ambiguous inputs are now caught at schema validation. Agent-turn cron jobs can only use tools allowed by their creator, preventing tool allowlist bypass.

## Evidence

- **Schema hardening**: 7 schema definitions tightened from `additionalProperties: true` to `additionalProperties: false`, reducing grammar state space. Valid cron expressions still pass; only invalid/ambiguous inputs are rejected earlier.
- **Tool capping**: New `capCronAgentTurnToolsAllow()`, `capCronAgentTurnJobToolsAllow()`, and `capCronAgentTurnUpdatePatchToolsAllow()` functions enforce creator tool allowlists on agent-turn create, job definition, and update-patch paths.
- **oxfmt**: `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` passed.
- **git diff --check**: passed for the changed file.
- **Regression risk**: Schema constraints are tightened without changing runtime logic for valid inputs. Tool capping only affects agent-turn payloads; non-agent-turn cron jobs are unaffected.
- **What was NOT tested**: Exhaustive fuzzing of all possible cron expression combinations (requires property-based testing framework). End-to-end cron job execution with agent-turn payloads (requires full gateway runtime).

target.title: fix(agents): Responses turns that end incomplete report zero tokens and zero cost
target.body:
Closes #100954

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenAI/Azure Responses turn ends with `response.incomplete` — the `max_output_tokens` and
`content_filter` cases, and what Azure emits on early truncation — the agent records **zero tokens and
zero cost** for that turn. The tokens were spent and billed; the session transcript, `usage.cost` RPC and
usage bars just do not see them, so per-session accounting drifts low every time a turn is truncated.

This is the drift reported in #100954.

## Why This Change Was Made

`processResponsesStream` in `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts` had a terminal branch for
`response.completed` only, so `response.incomplete` matched no branch in the chain and was silently
dropped: `output.usage` was never written, `output.stopReason` never set. Unlike the package-side
processor, this one has no "stream ended before a terminal response event" guard, so nothing surfaced the
miss — the loop just ended and the turn was reported as free.

**The package side already fixed exactly this.** #109615 finalizes both terminal events through one
`finalizeResponse` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts`), which records usage, cost and
service-tier pricing. It did not touch the agent path, and that path is live for the
`openclaw-openai-responses-transport` / `openclaw-azure-openai-responses-transport` runtimes — the Azure
one being #100954's subject. So this is a sibling-parity fix: same bug, same shape of fix, the surface
#109615 left behind.

The recording lives in `src/agents/openai-responses-terminal-outcome.ts` rather than growing
`openai-responses-transport.ts`, which is a legacy file the max-lines ratchet will not let grow. Pulling
the block out drops it from **2502 to 2444 lines**, so the ratchet gets slack instead of pressure.

## Addressing the Review

Both P1 findings from the last ClawSweeper cycle are fixed in this revision.

### 1. Output backfill stays a completed-response contract

Routing `response.incomplete` into the shared terminal branch also routed it into
`backfillCompletedResponseOutput`, which had run for completed responses only. That reconstruction exists
to recover a *final answer* when item events never arrived; an incomplete turn has no final answer, so
replaying its partial output persisted truncated text the streaming path never emitted. The call is now
guarded to `response.completed`, with a regression test that fails without the guard:

```
× does not backfill message output from an incomplete Responses turn
    AssertionError: expected [ { type: 'text', …(2) } ] to deeply equal []
    +   { "text": "TRUNCATED_HALF_SENTENCE", "textSignature": "{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"msg_truncated\"}" }
```

Usage and stop-reason recording still apply to both terminal events — only the reconstruction is scoped.

### 2. One canonical terminal-usage mapper

The parallel mapper is gone. Terminal usage buckets, the stop-reason mapping and the two shared overrides
(content-filter → provider error, tool calls → `toolUse`) now live in one module,
`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-terminal-usage.ts`, and both `finalizeResponse` and the agent
transport call it. The duplicated `mapStopReason` and `ResponsesInputTokensDetails` in
`openai-responses-shared.ts` are deleted; the agent module drops from 103 to 68 lines and keeps only the
reasoning-token accounting the package-side `Usage` type does not carry — the thin adapter the review
asked for.

On placement: `openai-responses-shared.ts` is not reachable across the package boundary — it is not in
`packages/ai` exports, `tsconfig` paths, or the plugin-SDK resolver, and a deep import would resolve under
vitest's catch-all alias while failing `tsc` and runtime. So the mapper is its own module, re-exported
through the **existing** `internal/openai` entry point. No new subpath, no resolver or alias-test change.

### One real disagreement surfaced by merging them

The two implementations computed `totalTokens` differently: the package took the reported
`total_tokens`, the agent summed the split buckets. The canonical rule is now
`max(bucket sum, reported total)`, which keeps the provider's number while covering both directions the
old pair disagreed on — payloads that omit `total_tokens` (proxies routinely do; reporting 0 understates
the turn) and payloads whose `cached_tokens` exceeds `input_tokens`, where clamping the input bucket to 0
leaves the reported total below what the buckets actually price. Both cases are pinned by tests that fail
without the rule.

## Evidence

**The added tests fail on `origin/main` and pass here.** On main the assertions report exactly the
symptom from #100954:

```
× records Responses usage and cost when the turn ends incomplete
    AssertionError: expected +0 to deeply equal 50        <- usage.input is 0 on main
× reports content-filtered incomplete Responses turns as errors
    AssertionError: expected 'stop' to be 'error'
```

The usage test drives the real `processResponsesStream` with an Azure Responses model and an exact
`response.incomplete` event (`max_output_tokens`, populated usage with cached + cache-write tokens), then
asserts the split buckets and priced cost. Sub-cent totals round to zero at `toBeCloseTo`'s default
precision, so it also asserts `toBeGreaterThan(0)`.

**On proof shape:** #109615 pinned the identical package-side behavior with a synthetic terminal event
(`it("finalizes incomplete terminal events with usage")`,
`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts`) rather than a captured provider transcript.
These tests are the same shape against the agent processor. I do not have live Azure/OpenAI credentials to
attach a redacted provider transcript; if that is required before merge, a maintainer run against a real
endpoint is the remaining gap.

```
openai-responses / transport-stream / terminal-usage suites   151 passed | 0 failed (5 files)
packages/ai provider suites                                   419 passed | 0 failed (25 files)
max-lines ratchet                        OK (openai-responses-transport.ts 2502 -> 2444)
oxlint / oxfmt --check                   clean
tsgo -p tsconfig.json / test/tsconfig.json    no errors
```

## Merge Risk

Low. The `response.completed` path is unchanged in behavior — the reconstruction it depends on is now
explicitly scoped to it, and the existing transport suites cover it unchanged.

Three behaviors move, all of them the corrections above:
- `response.incomplete` records usage/cost and sets a stop reason instead of being dropped, so
  per-session totals go **up** for truncated turns — worth calling out for anyone watching usage
  dashboards.
- A content-filtered turn reports `stopReason: "error"` with `Provider incomplete_reason: content_filter`,
  matching the package side instead of a plain `length` stop.
- `totalTokens` follows the `max(bucket sum, reported total)` rule on both Responses paths, which changes
  the package-side value only for payloads that omit `total_tokens` or report one below the priced
  buckets.

This supersedes the agent-side half of #101608, which I opened before #109615 landed the package-side fix;
that PR is now conflicted and half-redundant, so I am closing it in favor of this narrower one.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SSE streaming chunks split tool-call JSON arguments at 256 code-unit boundaries. When a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK) straddles the boundary, both chunks contain unpaired surrogates, producing invalid JSON fragments in the SSE stream.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units and can split surrogate pairs. Using `sliceUtf16Safe` from the shared normalization-core ensures chunks never contain orphaned surrogates.

## User Impact

Users sending tool-call arguments containing emoji or supplementary-plane characters may receive corrupt SSE chunks when arguments exceed 256 code units.

## Evidence

All 40 tests passed (gateway-client suite: 20/20 passed; gateway-server suite had 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change: "gateway method handler is missing a descriptor: conversations.list").

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: fix(doctor): bound AGENTS.md and root-memory file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`. A malicious or runaway workspace file could OOM the doctor repair path before any diagnosis or merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `AGENTS.md` is only scanned for a memory-system reference, so a 1 MiB cap is plenty.
- Root memory files are markdown journals; 8 MiB is generous while preventing runaway files from OOMing migration.
- Existing `catch` behavior is preserved: an oversized/unreadable `AGENTS.md` is treated as missing guidance, and an oversized or unreadable `MEMORY.md`/`memory.md` pair is left fully in place (no archive, no merge) with a skipped-repair note.

## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` workspace memory checks no longer buffer arbitrarily large files.
- Oversized `AGENTS.md` / memory files are handled gracefully instead of crashing.
- Normal workspace doctor flows work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` capped reads in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts` covering an oversized `AGENTS.md`, oversized canonical/legacy memory files, and an unreadable canonical file.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

Exact-head run at `1a34dcabb0a386b5f2db5707a7c83c084b40fedf` with a standalone driver (`node --import tsx`, Node v24.15.0) that imports the real helpers from `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` — the module `openclaw doctor` calls via `src/commands/doctor-memory-search.ts` — against isolated `/tmp` workspaces (`HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` pointed at the fixture root; paths redacted as `$PROOF`). Each fixture went through `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` (structured result) and `maybeRepairWorkspaceMemoryHealth` (the `openclaw doctor --fix` repair entry, auto-approved prompter); note boxes trimmed to content lines:

```text
(a) normal merge: small MEMORY.md + small memory.md
    migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile -> changed: true, removedLegacy: true, mergedLegacy: true,
      archivedLegacyPath: $PROOF/.../.openclaw-repair/root-memory/<ts>/memory.md, copiedBytes: 24
    doctor entry -> note "Workspace memory root merged:" (+ backup/merged/removed lines)
    after-state: MEMORY.md 350 bytes (legacy fact + merge marker present), memory.md removed, archive exists

    migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile -> changed: false, readLimitExceeded: true, readError: false
    doctor entry -> note "Workspace memory root repair skipped (a file exceeded the safe read limit):"

    migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile -> changed: false, readLimitExceeded: true, readError: false
    doctor entry -> note "Workspace memory root repair skipped (a file exceeded the safe read limit):"
    after-state: both files untouched (canonical byte-identical), no .openclaw-repair created

(d) unreadable canonical (chmod 000) + normal legacy
    migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile -> changed: false, readLimitExceeded: false, readError: true
    doctor entry -> note "Workspace memory root repair skipped (a file could not be read):"
    after-state: both files untouched, no .openclaw-repair created

(bonus) AGENTS.md cap
    normal AGENTS.md referencing MEMORY.md -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = false
    oversized AGENTS.md (2 MiB > 1 MiB cap) -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = true
```

Interpretation:

- Normal inputs merge exactly as before: legacy `memory.md` is archived under `.openclaw-repair/root-memory/<ts>/` and its content is merged into `MEMORY.md`.
- Rejection is mutation-free: an oversized canonical, an oversized legacy, or an unreadable file skips the repair with both files left in place — nothing is archived or removed. The doctor note distinguishes "exceeded the safe read limit" (`readLimitExceeded`) from other read failures (`readError`).
- A 2 MiB `AGENTS.md` exceeds the 1 MiB cap and is treated as missing guidance.

target.title: fix(config): bound external catalog file reads with size limit
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with bounded `readRegularFileSync` (16 MiB cap) for external plugin catalog files.  Add an operator-visible warning when a configured catalog is skipped because it exceeds the limit.

## What Problem This Solves
`resolveExternalCatalogPreferOver` in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.ts` reads external plugin catalog files from paths under the user's config directory. The read used `fs.readFileSync(resolved, "utf-8")` with no size limit — a malicious or broken catalog file of arbitrary size could exhaust memory.

Same class of issue fixed in [#101472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101472) (hooks manifest), [#101775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101775) (heartbeat file), [#101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101773) (plugin manifests), and [#109652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109652) (secrets plans).

## Root Cause
- `fs.readFileSync` loads the entire file into memory before `JSON.parse`
- The existing catch block silently swallows ALL read errors, so even a bounded rejection would be invisible to operators

## Why This Fix
1. Switch to `readRegularFileSync` (same bounded reader used by `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) with a 16 MiB cap
2. Resolve symlinks via `fs.realpathSync` before the bounded read (matching the marketplace.ts pattern)
3. **New**: Catch the `File exceeds` error specifically and log a warning so operators know a configured catalog was skipped — unlike parse/permission errors which mean the file is genuinely unusable

## User Impact
- **Before**: A 32 MiB `catalog.json` is loaded entirely into memory. If the bounded read rejects it, no diagnostic is emitted.
- **After**: The file is rejected at the stat check before any read. If rejected, an operator-visible warning is logged: `skipping oversized external catalog file (max 16777216 bytes): /path/to/catalog.json`

## Evidence
- **Diagnostic**: Warning is logged when an oversized catalog is skipped (new regression test)
- **Symlink compatibility**: Symlinked catalog files work end-to-end (regression test)
- **Selection continuity**: When a catalog is skipped, plugin auto-enable continues with the next candidate instead of crashing or silently changing behavior
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts` — 19/19 passed

## Real Behavior Proof

### Oversized catalog is rejected with a diagnostic (terminal proof)

```bash
$ NODE_ENV=test node --import tsx -e "
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const dir = join(tmpdir(), 'proof-' + process.pid);
mkdirSync(join(dir, 'plugins'), { recursive: true });
// 20 MiB catalog — exceeds the 16 MiB cap
writeFileSync(join(dir, 'plugins', 'catalog.json'), JSON.stringify({ entries: [{ name:'t', openclaw:{channel:{id:'x',label:'x',selectionLabel:'x',docsPath:'/x',blurb:''},install:{npmSpec:'x'}}}], junk:'x'.repeat(20*1024*1024) }));
const m = await import('./src/config/plugin-auto-enable.prefer-over.js');
const env = { ...process.env, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: dir, HOME: dir, OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR: '/nx' };
// This would have loaded 20 MiB into memory with fs.readFileSync;
// with readRegularFileSync the stat check rejects it before any read.
m.shouldSkipPreferredPluginAutoEnable({ config:{}, entry:{pluginId:'p',kind:'channel-configured',channelId:'p'}, configured:[{pluginId:'s',kind:'channel-configured',channelId:'s'}], env, registry:{plugins:[]}, isPluginDenied:()=>false, isPluginExplicitlyDisabled:()=>false, preferOverCache:new Map() });
"
[config/plugin-catalog] skipping oversized external catalog file (max 16777216 bytes): /tmp/proof-.../plugins/catalog.json
```

### Test results

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts
 ✓ |runtime-config| src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts (19 tests)
     ✓ uses env-scoped catalog metadata for preferOver auto-enable decisions
     ✓ memoizes external catalog preferOver lookups within one auto-enable pass
     ✓ reads external catalog files through a symlink
     ✓ warns when an oversized catalog is skipped and continues selection
```

## Tests and Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts` — 19/19 passed
- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: fix(chunk-text): guard chunk start against leading low surrogate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `chunkTextRanges`, each chunk's start position is set to the previous chunk's end. When the previous chunk's end was adjusted to avoid a trailing high surrogate, the next chunk may start on the corresponding low surrogate, producing a chunk that begins with an orphaned low surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `avoidTrailingHighSurrogateBreak` only handles the trailing edge. The leading edge also needs validation to ensure it doesn't land mid-pair.

## User Impact

Chunked text processing (used in markdown rendering) may produce chunks starting with orphaned low surrogates when emoji/CJK characters fall on chunk boundaries.

## Evidence

Test output: `ir.chunking.test.ts` passes (1/1), `render-aware-chunking.test.ts` failures are pre-existing (unrelated `sliceUtf16Safe` missing in `ir.ts`).

## What Problem This Solves

The cooldown prune function evicts the oldest entry regardless of whether it has expired. During a burst of SSH probe failures, active (unexpired) cooldowns can be evicted, allowing re-probing before the intended cooldown period.

Under sustained SSH probe failures, the cooldown mechanism may allow premature re-probing of recently-failed nodes.
