target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (extracted to `packages/media-core`) that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
  - Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop before decode
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Codex OAuth image result route guard (ClawSweeper P1)

The reviewer flagged that the documented Codex OAuth Responses route (`extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`) returned a base64 `b64_json` image result and needed the configured byte budget applied before decode. At the current head this is guarded end to end. Source trace of the exact-head control flow:

- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1044` — `const maxImageBytes = resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(req.cfg)` (resolved from `cfg.agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, else `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`).
- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1049-1059` — the response is parsed with `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse(data, { ..., maxBytes: maxImageBytes })`. **This `maxBytes` argument is new vs `upstream/main`** (main's call site does not pass `maxBytes`).
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:221` — `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` accepts `maxBytes` and forwards it to `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:199-219` — forwards `maxBytes` to `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:150-155` — `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes(base64)` and returns `undefined` (drops the entry, no `Buffer.from` decode) when `estimatedSize > params.maxBytes`.

So an oversized Codex OAuth `b64_json` result is dropped **before** base64 decode, with no allocation of the decoded buffer. The guard is applied on the exact OAuth result path the reviewer named.

Exact-head runtime output (synthetic controlled payloads via in-repo boundary tests):
```
# src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts (added this head)
- "drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)"
    -> 2-entry response: small (accepted) + 200-char base64 over 10-byte cap (dropped)
    -> images.length === 1, images[0].buffer === "tiny"
```

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: boundary tests in `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB
  - Codex OAuth route: oversized `b64_json` entry dropped before decode when `maxBytes` set

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Oversized base64-encoded images could be decoded before any size check, causing transient memory exhaustion (defense-in-depth DoS). The fix estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` and rejects over-limit input **before** decoding in `writeCliImages` (CLI staging), `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` (provider image parsing), and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`), propagating the existing `maxBytes`/`generatedMediaMaxBytes` limit.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The guard is exercised by the in-repo boundary tests that feed controlled base64 payloads (7MB / 8MB / 10MB) and assert accept/reject decisions before decode, plus the new route-level test for the Codex OAuth path.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
 - rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
 - accepts 7MB payload under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
 - rejects 10MB payload under 8MB limit
 - rejects 7MB payload under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
 - drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)
```

Observed result after fix: Payloads exceeding the configured/default media size limit are rejected before any `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` decode, so oversized input cannot trigger transient memory pressure. Configured limits above the default are honored. The Codex OAuth image-generation result route now applies the same `maxBytes` budget before decoding. No new configuration surface was added (uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes`).

What was not tested: Live provider out-of-memory reproduction was not run (neither necessary nor safely desirable — the reviewer agreed); the proof targets the exact changed guard branches with synthetic over-limit payloads.

target.title: fix(agents): agent-created files get lowercased names on Windows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, files and directories an agent creates get **lowercased names**. Ask for
`src/Components/MyComponent.tsx` and what lands on disk is `src\components\mycomponent.tsx`.

NTFS is case-insensitive but case-*preserving*, so nothing fails locally — the agent reads its own file
back fine. The damage shows up downstream: git records the lowercased name, and the TypeScript/React
import the agent just wrote (`./Components/MyComponent`) resolves on the author's Windows box but breaks
for every teammate on Linux/macOS and in CI. Any agent-authored name that is not already lowercase is
affected: `README.md`, `Dockerfile`, `MyClass.ts`.

For some names it is worse than a case change. `"İstanbul.md".toLowerCase()` is `"i̇stanbul.md"` —
U+0130 becomes the two code points U+0069 U+0307, one longer than the original and not reversible. So a
Turkish filename does not come back lowercased, it comes back **corrupted**.

This is Windows-only. The POSIX branch of the same function preserves case correctly today.

## Why This Change Was Made

`toRelativePathUnderRoot` (`src/agents/path-policy.ts:76-90`) ran both root and candidate through
`normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` and then **returned** the resulting relative path:

```ts
const rootForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(rootResolved);
const targetForCompare = normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(resolvedCandidate);
const relative = path.win32.relative(rootForCompare, targetForCompare);
return validateRelativePathWithinBoundary({ relativePath: relative, ... });
```

That helper lowercases (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1`, `dist/path.js:17` →
`normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(...)`). Lowercasing is right for a **comparison key** — which is exactly
how the other two call sites use it — but this function hands the relative path back to callers, and they
build files out of it:

- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1089-1092` — `mkdir`: `path.resolve(root, relative)` → `fs.mkdir`
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts:1059-1060` — `writeWorkspaceFile` → `.write(relative, { mkdir: true })`
- `src/agents/apply-patch.ts:310,318,326` — `apply_patch` writeFile / remove / mkdirp

`toCanonicalRelativeWorkspacePath` (`agent-tools.read.ts:1167-1179`) does not rescue it: `fs.realpath`
restores the true case only of the **already-existing** ancestor, the new basename stays lowercased, and
line 1179 re-lowercases the whole thing on the way out. `assertSandboxPath` does not either — it is
handed the already-derived `resolved` path, not the original candidate.

The lowercasing was also never needed for the boundary math. `path.win32.relative` already matches the
root case-insensitively **and** returns the tail in its original case, so the pre-lowercasing bought
nothing and cost the filename. The one part of that normalization the boundary check does rely on is
extended-length prefix stripping — without it a `\\?\C:\...` candidate relativizes to
`..\..\..\?\C:\...` and gets rejected as an escape. So this adds `normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase`
next to the comparison variant in `src/infra/path-guards.ts`. It mirrors that helper step for step —
including the trim — minus the lowercasing, and a test pins that equivalence directly so the two cannot
drift:

```ts
expect(normalizeWindowsPathPreservingCase(input).toLowerCase()).toBe(
  normalizeWindowsPathForComparison(input),
);
```

### Sibling surfaces

All three callers of `normalizeWindowsPathForComparison` were checked. Only this one was misusing it:

| Call site | Uses result as | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts:215` | comparison key (`===`) | correct, untouched |
| `isPathInside` (fs-safe) | discards relative, returns boolean | correct, untouched |
| `src/agents/path-policy.ts` | **returns it to callers** | fixed here |

## Evidence

**Live before/after on real Windows** (Windows 11, NTFS, Turkish locale), driving the real
`toRelativeWorkspacePath` through the exact call pattern of `agent-tools.read.ts`, then reading the names
back with `fs.readdirSync`:

Before (`origin/main`):

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---
  toRelativeWorkspacePath -> "src\components\mycomponent.tsx"
  ON DISK                 -> components/mycomponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md  | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : i̇stanbul.md | length 12 | U+0069 U+0307
  identical? NO  <- filename corrupted, not just lowercased
```

```
--- case 1: agent asked for src\Components\MyComponent.tsx ---

  ON DISK                 -> Components/MyComponent.tsx

--- case 2: agent asked for İstanbul.md ---
  asked   : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130
  ON DISK : İstanbul.md | length 11 | U+0130 U+0073
  identical? YES
```

**Why the existing test did not catch it:** `path-policy.test.ts:23` used an all-lowercase candidate
(`c:/users/user/openclaw/memory/log.txt`), which passes either way. The new cases use mixed case.

**Tests** — every added mixed-case assertion fails on `origin/main` and passes here:


Low, but this touches a sandbox boundary, so here is the containment argument explicitly.

**The boundary decision is unchanged.** `path.win32.relative` compares case-insensitively, so

```

root itself, differing case   -> ""                     allowRoot still honored
drive-letter case c: vs C:    -> "Memory\Log.txt"       still matched
\\?\ prefix NOT stripped      -> "..\..\..\?\C:\..."    why stripping is kept
```

Two of the added tests pin this directly — an escape that differs from the root only by case is still
rejected, and a differently-cased root still resolves to `""` under `allowRoot`. Both pass before and

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup could leave channel shutdown waiting forever. The race occurs when the gateway stop signal is already aborted before the monitor registers its listener, or becomes aborted while startup allowlist/group resolution is in progress.

The monitor now checks for shutdown before asynchronous startup work and rechecks after that work before creating the Zalo listener. target.title: fix(ci): bound docs-sync publish repo git fetch with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The two `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` calls in `.github/workflows/docs-sync-publish.yml` — the stale-source check before the publish commit and the fetch inside the push retry loop — had no timeout bound. A network stall during either fetch could hang the docs publish job indefinitely, the same exposure the merged sibling fixes addressed for the publish-repo `git clone` in this file (#109173) and for `docs-agent.yml` fetches (#110026).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fetches now run under `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s`, the exact wrapper shape already merged for this file's clone (#109173), `docs-agent.yml` (#110026), `linux-app-release.yml` (#110027), and `macos-release.yml` (#109174). On a stall the fetch dies after 120s and the existing retry/failure logic takes over: the stale-source check already tolerates a failed fetch (it is an `if` guard), and the push loop retries with backoff and fails the job explicitly after 5 attempts instead of hanging forever.

## Changes

- Wrap both `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` invocations with `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` (2 lines).

## User Impact

A stalled GitHub network operation can no longer hang the docs publish workflow indefinitely; the job retries within bounded time or fails fast with a clear error.

## Evidence

Exact head: a6b076ffc59e7b172c20c63e945e61861b496c2d.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and truncate to 20 in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior. Per reviewer feedback, the Matrix boundary **truncates** options > 20 (keeps the first 20) rather than throwing, so existing callers with more than 20 options still produce a valid `m.poll.start` event instead of failing closed.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` slices options to `MATRIX_POLL_MAX_OPTIONS` before normalizing
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, truncate 21→20)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and truncation in `buildPollStartContent`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.
- **P1: Provide real behavior proof (not only unit tests)** — Added a runtime trace that drives the real production boundaries for both the 20 (accepted) and 21 (truncated) paths. See "Runtime behavior trace" below.
- **Reviewer follow-up: prefer truncation over fail-closed** — Changed the Matrix boundary from throwing on > 20 options to truncating to the first 20 options (MSC3381 max), so callers with more than 20 options still emit a valid poll event. The previously failing test now asserts truncation.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now declared at the Matrix boundary and options beyond 20 are truncated to the protocol maximum.
- **Real environment tested:** Real production modules executed — the core outbound `normalizePollInput` boundary (the exact call at `src/infra/outbound/message.ts:510` and `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts:1021`) and the Matrix `buildPollStartContent` m.poll.start builder, plus Vitest regression tests.

### Runtime behavior trace

Drove the real production paths for both the 20-option (success) and 21-option (truncated) cases, with `maxOptions` sourced from the Matrix outbound `pollMaxOptions = 20`. Captured output:

```text
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(20, maxOptions=20) -> options.length=20
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(21, maxOptions=20) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(20) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20, last id=answer20
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(21) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20 (truncated), first=Option 1, last=Option 20
```

- 20 options: accepted end to end; the Matrix builder emits 20 `m.poll.start` answers (`answer1`..`answer20`).
- 21 options: the core outbound `normalizePollInput` (which is caller-controlled and keeps the original fail-closed contract when `maxOptions` is supplied) throws; the Matrix builder path **truncates** to the first 20 options and emits a valid `m.poll.start` event instead of throwing. This keeps the Matrix channel operational for callers that pass more than 20 options.

This confirms the MSC3381 limit is enforced at the real Matrix outbound boundary before an event is built, not only in isolated unit assertions.

- **Exact commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/polls.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # src/polls.test.ts — 7 passed
  - "does not limit options when maxOptions is omitted" → 50 options accepted ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 10 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "truncates to 20 poll options per MSC3381 instead of rejecting" → answers.length = 20, first=Option 1, last=Option 20 ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts — 6 passed
  - "declares a 20-option poll maximum..." → outbound.pollMaxOptions = 20 ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary via truncation. Public helper contract preserved (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + runtime boundary trace
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 truncated to 20 (protocol boundary in `buildPollStartContent`)
  - Matrix outbound: `pollMaxOptions = 20` declared on static adapter
  - Public helper: omitted `maxOptions` does not limit (contract preserved)

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Matrix outbound adapter did not declare `pollMaxOptions`, unlike all other poll channel adapters (Discord, WhatsApp, MS Teams, Telegram).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No Matrix-owned poll option limit enforcement.

target.title: fix(discord): refresh member roles after join or leave
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord users who leave or rejoin a guild can retain stale cached member roles for up to 30 seconds. During that interval, role-based Discord voice admission can evaluate the user's previous membership state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord now invalidates cached member and user entities for `GUILD_MEMBER_ADD` and `GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE`, matching the existing `GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE` behavior. The change stays inside the Discord plugin cache boundary and does not add configuration, compatibility shims, or per-event allocations.

## User Impact

Discord role changes caused by leaving or joining a guild are reflected on the next member lookup instead of waiting for the REST cache TTL. This prevents removed or rejoined users from being authorized with stale role data.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A cached Discord guild member survives add/remove Gateway lifecycle events on current `main`; the next member lookup therefore reuses stale roles instead of querying Discord REST.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0. Baseline `923d92bdd0e3ddb978ab566efe29a737dc204edf`; exact PR head `2c2f32886853a9ef604098d7238c0a8b8768ab2b`.
- **Exact steps or command run:** `HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx --input-type=module` with an inline script importing the production `DiscordEntityCache`, warming its member/user entries, delivering each real `GatewayDispatchEvents` member lifecycle constant, and repeating both production lookups.
- **Evidence before fix:** Terminal capture of the `node` source-runtime probe on current `main` (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  GUILD_MEMBER_ADD: before=2 after=2 STALE
  GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE: before=2 after=2 STALE
  GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE: before=2 after=4 PASS
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the same `node` source-runtime probe on the exact PR head (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  GUILD_MEMBER_ADD: before=2 after=4 PASS
  GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE: before=2 after=4 PASS
  GUILD_MEMBER_UPDATE: before=2 after=4 PASS
  exact_head=2c2f32886853a9ef604098d7238c0a8b8768ab2b
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Add, remove, and update events all evict the member and user entities. The next `fetchMember()` and `fetchUser()` calls reach Discord REST instead of reusing the warmed entries.
- **What was not tested:** A live Discord member leave/rejoin followed by a voice role-admission attempt was not run. That test requires a disposable human/user-driver identity that can leave and rejoin through an invite. The repository's Discord QA credential contract provides only two bots already installed in the shared guild (`driverBotToken` and `sutBotToken`); removing either bot is not safely reversible by the current runner.

### Maintainer live gate

The existing `qa discord` scenarios cover canary messaging, mention gating, command registration, voice auto-join, reactions, and attachment flows. None changes guild membership. A safe live proof needs a disposable user, not either shared QA bot:

1. Start this exact PR head with Discord Gateway logging, Server Members Intent, and a voice-channel role allowlist enabled.
2. Give the disposable user the allowed role, enter the configured voice channel, and complete one admitted voice turn to warm the member REST cache.
3. Have that user leave the guild and rejoin through a retained invite without the allowed role.
4. Record redacted `GUILD_MEMBER_REMOVE` and `GUILD_MEMBER_ADD` observations, the next member REST lookup, and the subsequent denied voice admission.
5. Redact guild, channel, user, endpoint, invite, and credential data before attaching the terminal output or recording.

Current automated QA cannot perform steps 3-4 because the Discord Convex payload has no rejoinable user credential or invite field. Expanding that credential contract and runner would be a separate QA infrastructure change, not part of this two-file cache fix.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       7 passed (7)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/entity-cache.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# no output
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two child-session (subagent) issues in the sidebar tree, continuing the quiet-sidebar series (#110448/#110459/#110470/#110524):
1. A parent with many subagents dumps its full child list into the sidebar — potentially dozens of rows.
2. Every child row carried the hardcoded "Subagent:" prefix (`session-display.ts` prepends it), which is redundant under an indented child row and truncates the actual title ("Subagent: Reading rec…").

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer request: show at most 4 children with a muted "Show {count} more" affordance, and drop the prefix where the hierarchy is already visible.

## User Impact

- Expanded parents show the first 4 children plus a gray "Show N more" row; clicking reveals the full list for that parent. Collapsing the parent's children resets the cap. Works per level for nested trees.
- The cap never hides what matters: the active session's branch (`visuallyActive`/`containsActiveDescendant`) and any branch with live runs (`hasActiveRun`/`status running`/transitive `runningChildCount`) always render, even past the cap.
- Child rows in the tree render their real title without "Subagent:"; flat surfaces (palette, search, chat header) keep the prefix via the default of the new `includeSubagentPrefix` option. Untitled subagents keep the "Subagent:" fallback rather than rendering an empty row.
- One new i18n key `sessionsView.showMoreChildren` (English source; locales are bot-generated).

![child row without prefix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/quiet-sidebar/child-noprefix.png)

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts` — 109 pass, including new cases: 6-child parent shows 4 + "Show 2 more"; reveal-all; collapse-reset; unprefixed child labels; and a quiet child past the cap with a running grandchild stays visible ("Show 1 more").
- `ui/src/lib/session-display.test.ts` — 11 pass (prefix default, opt-out, fallback).
- Live-verified in the mock harness: child row reads "Reading receipts" (screenshot above; fixture has one child, so cap behavior is proven by tests).
- Codex autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol), three rounds: round 1 found the cap could hide the active session's branch — fixed; round 2 found nested running descendants could hide behind the cap — fixed via transitive runningChildCount; round 3's remaining claim (base-class TS2339) was verified false: the list element inherits from the navigation element (List → Menus → Groups → Mutations → Navigation), the same relationship existing `isSessionChildrenExpanded` calls use.

target.title: fix: bound miscellaneous unbounded file reads across 5 modules
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Five modules use unbounded fs.readFileSync/fs.promises.readFile calls on user-controlled file paths. A corrupted or oversized file at any of these paths can OOM the process:

1. **src/plugins/bundle-commands.ts** — plugin bundle command markdown
2. **src/cli/config-set-input.ts** — CLI batch files
3. **src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts** — AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md
4. **src/trajectory/cleanup.ts** — trajectory pointer JSON
5. **src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts** — diagnostic config export

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established readRegularFileSync/readRegularFile with maxBytes as the standard bounded-read primitive. These five sites were the remaining unbounded read calls on user-controlled file paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Each file type has a generous cap (1-10 MB). Files exceeding the cap produce graceful error/fallback instead of crashing.

## Evidence

### Pattern (same for all 5 files)
Each file replaces `fs.readFileSync(path, encoding)` or `fs.promises.readFile(path, encoding)` with:
```ts
const { buffer } = readRegularFileSync({ filePath: path, maxBytes: LIMIT });
const content = buffer.toString("utf-8");
```

### Changes by file
| File | Old | New | Cap | Error Handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bundle-commands.ts | fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 1 MB | RangeError → skip file |
| config-set-input.ts | fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 8 MB | RangeError → descriptive error |
| doctor-workspace.ts (3x) | fs.promises.readFile(path, "utf-8") | readRegularFile + buffer.toString | 10 MB | .catch → empty buffer fallback |
| cleanup.ts | fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 1 MB | existing try-catch → null |
| diagnostic-support-export.ts | fs.readFileSync(configPath, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 8 MB | existing catch → config failure |

### Fixes Applied
- **2026-07-18**: Fixed ClawSweeper P1 finding — all 5 files now correctly destructure `{ buffer }` from the readRegularFile result before calling .toString() (previously the return value was used directly)
- Branch rebased onto current main

### Provenance
Follows PR #101472 (merged) and PR #101477 patterns.

target.title: fix(canvas): stop sending undefined coords on partial placement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent calls `canvas present` with only a subset of placement coordinates (e.g. only `width` and `height`), the old code constructed a placement object with `undefined` values for the missing fields. `JSON.stringify` silently strips `undefined` keys, so the node receives incomplete placement data.

## Root Cause

`readFiniteNumberParam` returns `undefined` for absent keys. The code at `tool.ts:122-140` unconditionally set all four fields then checked `Number.isFinite` on each to decide whether to include placement at all — but when some are finite and some aren't, the whole object (with undefined entries) is sent downstream.

## Fix

Only defined placement values are collected into the `placement` record. The gate check uses `Object.keys(placement).length > 0` instead of four individual `Number.isFinite` checks.

Files changed:
- `extensions/canvas/src/tool.ts`: Refactored `case "present"` placement construction

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Partial placement coords no longer send `undefined` to the node
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff main --check -- extensions/canvas/` — clean
  - `npx vitest run extensions/canvas/src/tool.test.ts` — 12 passed, 1 skipped (symlink on Windows)
- Observed result: All existing tests pass. Placement object now only contains defined coordinates, preventing silent `undefined` propagation through JSON serialization.

target.title: fix(agents): route llama.cpp GBNF cleaning through provider tool-schema hooks
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp-backed endpoint with grammar-constrained tool calling, chat requests fail with HTTP 400 before inference whenever the active tool list includes GBNF-hostile JSON Schema constructs (#108580):

1. Unanchored / PCRE-shorthand `pattern` (e.g. `\\S`)
2. `maxLength` above llama.cpp's ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling (e.g. cron `trigger.script` `65536`)

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical tool schemas keep their server-side validation guidance. Cleaning happens only on llama.cpp-compatible routes:

| Activation path | Who owns it |
|---|---|
| Bundled `ollama`, `ollama-cloud`, `lmstudio`, `llama-cpp` | Provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` via `buildProviderToolCompatFamilyHooks("llamacpp-gbnf")` |
| Custom OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp endpoints | Opt-in `modelCompat.toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` |
| Ordinary providers (`openai`, etc.) | Unchanged — canonical `pattern` / `maxLength` retained |

Shared-core provider-ID guessing was removed (ClawSweeper P1). This mirrors the Gemini family-helper pattern in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-tools`.

## User Impact

llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio users can keep cron and related tools enabled without pre-inference grammar 400s. OpenAI and other providers keep model-facing length/pattern constraints.

## Evidence

### Exact-head bundled-provider live proof (head `9ac84e3e042`)

This run registered the real bundled Ollama plugin, selected its provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` hook, printed the outbound schema, and sent that schema to a local `llama-server` b9960. Private endpoint details are omitted.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/exact-head-gbnf-live-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
EXACT_HEAD=9ac84e3e042
PROVIDER_HOOK=ollama
OUTBOUND_SCHEMA={"type":"object","properties":{"declarationKey":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":200},"script":{"type":"string","minLength":1}}}
LLAMA_SERVER_HTTP=200
INFERENCE_RESPONSE={"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"ready"}}],...}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

This proves the current bundled-provider activation path: `pattern` and oversized `maxLength: 65536` are absent from the outbound schema, `maxLength: 200` remains, and llama-server successfully reaches inference.

### Focused tests
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/clean-for-llamacpp-gbnf.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.llamacpp.test.ts \
```

All green on Node 22.

### Live llama-server regression transcript (shipped failure)
Earlier local `llama-server` b9960 run against the shipped grammar-hostile cron schema:

- unanchored `\\S` → HTTP 400 `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`
- `maxLength: 65536` → HTTP 400 `failed to parse grammar`
- cleaned schema (same projection the provider hook now emits) → HTTP 200, inference proceeds

The cleaned payload that reached HTTP 200 is exactly what `normalizeLlamacppGbnfToolSchemas` / `toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` emit on this head.

### vs #108671
#108671 removes constraints from canonical tool schemas globally. This PR preserves them and cleans only on llama.cpp-compatible provider/profile routes — the ownership ClawSweeper recommended.

target.title: fix(canvas): classify deleteSurface and dataModelUpdate as v0.9-only actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` are A2UI v0.9 actions — only `surfaceUpdate` and `beginRendering` exist in v0.8. But the validator only checked for `createSurface` as a v0.9 indicator. Unversioned `deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` payloads were incorrectly classified as v0.8 and passed validation, then sent to the native client which cannot process them.

The native client's own schema confirms these are protocol-level action keys:
```js
// a2ui.bundle.js:4087
message: "A2UI Protocol message must have exactly one of: surfaceUpdate, dataModelUpdate, beginRendering, deleteSurface."
```

## Root Cause

`a2ui-jsonl.ts:88` — `if (explicitVersion === "v0.9" || actionKeys[0] === "createSurface")` — only `createSurface` triggered v0.9 detection. `deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` fell through to `sawV08 = true`.

## Fix

Added `V09_ONLY_ACTIONS` set covering all three v0.9-only action keys: `createSurface`, `deleteSurface`, `dataModelUpdate`. The condition now uses `V09_ONLY_ACTIONS.has(actionKeys[0] ?? "")`.

Files changed:
- `extensions/canvas/src/a2ui-jsonl.ts`: Added `V09_ONLY_ACTIONS` set, updated detection condition
- `extensions/canvas/src/tool.test.ts`: Added two regression test cases

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Unversioned `deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` now correctly classified as v0.9 and rejected
- Commands / artifacts:

## What Problem This Solves

When `canvas.eval` returns a non-string result or error from the node (e.g. `{ payload: { error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token" } }`), the old code returned `jsonResult({ ok: true })` — a generic success signal. The agent sees success even when the JavaScript evaluation failed.

- Type cast widened to `{ payload?: { result?: unknown; error?: string } }`
- Non-string results return `{ ok: false, error, result }` so error context is visible to the agent
- String results are unchanged (existing behavior preserved)

target.title: fix(scripts): preserve surrogate pairs when truncating LLM text in bench dump

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation. Collision check: no open same-file or same-problem PR was found.

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

target.title: fix(zalouser): settle waitForExit when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stopping a ZaloUser gateway account during or immediately after connection startup could leave channel shutdown waiting forever. The race occurs when the gateway stop signal is already aborted before the monitor registers its listener, or becomes aborted while startup allowlist/group resolution is in progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`AbortSignal` does not replay an `abort` event to listeners registered after the signal has fired. The monitor now checks for shutdown before asynchronous startup work and rechecks after that work before creating the Zalo listener. The existing listener lifecycle remains local to listener startup; no extra lifecycle state is introduced.

The fix stays inside the ZaloUser plugin and adds no config, protocol, SDK, dependency, or compatibility surface.

## User Impact

ZaloUser stop and restart operations now settle promptly instead of hanging during fast gateway restarts or overlapping account lifecycle transitions. An aborted startup also cannot restore a Zalo listener session.

## Evidence

The dedicated lifecycle suite follows the production gateway boundary (`zalouserPlugin.gateway.startAccount` -> `monitorZalouserProvider`) and mocks only the outer Zalo SDK/network boundary. It proves:

- normal startup remains pending until abort, then invokes the listener's `stop` exactly once and settles;
- shutdown during the pending friends-resolution Promise completes without restoring `startZaloListener`;
- an already-aborted signal skips monitor preflight and listener startup;
- failure-path cleanup always aborts and settles test tasks, preventing leaked Promises or cross-test pollution.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin/main@347ee45895` | 1 passed, 2 failed | Calls `startZaloListener` after mid-preflight abort; calls `listZaloFriends` after pre-abort |
| refreshed PR head `e49cbc2f2c` | 3 passed, 0 failed | Both invalid startup paths are skipped; normal abort/stop lifecycle still passes |

target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The gateway's WebSocket upgrade currently admits every connection and only checks the browser `Origin` *after* the HTTP 101 handshake completes. Any client that reaches the upgrade — including a cross-origin browser page or a scripted WebSocket — gets a live socket before origin policy is enforced, and the rejection happens post-handshake. For a gateway that fronts operator control UI and agent sessions, the origin check should run as a pre-handshake gate so an unauthorized origin never completes the upgrade.

This change adds a `verifyClient` hook to the gateway `WebSocketServer` (wired at `server-runtime-state.ts:281`) that runs the **existing** `checkBrowserOrigin` — the same function the post-handshake admission path already uses — *before* the 101 response. No new origin policy is introduced; the pre-handshake and post-handshake paths now share one source of truth (`gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` / `dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`).

## Why this change was made

- **Close the pre-auth window.** A disallowed browser origin is rejected with `403` during `verifyClient`, not after the socket opens.
- **Reuse, don't reinvent.** `checkBrowserOrigin` is already the production origin contract; this moves where it runs, not how it decides.
- **No new config keys.** The gate reads existing `gateway.controlUi.*` settings. No `gateway.security.*`, forwarded-header, or `Sec-Fetch-Site` logic is added — keeping the change to a single, proven control.
- **Non-browser clients are unaffected when they send no `Origin`.** CLI / native apps pass through exactly as today; they continue to authenticate post-handshake.

## User Impact

- Operators with `allowedOrigins` set: cross-origin browser pages are now rejected at the handshake instead of after it. Behavior for allowed origins and for CLI/native clients (no `Origin`) is unchanged.
- No config migration, no new settings, no breaking changes to existing deployments *for the no-Origin client path*.

## CSRF note (no regression vs today)

This gate does **not** add a separate `Sec-Fetch-Site` check. A same-origin-only deployment still relies on `allowedOrigins` for cross-site WebSocket defense — which is exactly the contract the post-handshake admission path already enforces today. Moving the check to pre-handshake does not weaken that contract; it only runs it earlier. There is **no regression** versus prior behavior *for the browser/Control-UI/webchat path this gate targets*.

## Compatibility / Scope Decision Needed (reviewer asks)

The pre-handshake gate runs `checkBrowserOrigin` on **every request that carries an `Origin` header**. The current post-handshake admission path (`connect-admission.ts`) scopes origin enforcement to `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient || isBrowserOperatorUi || isWebchat`, where `enforceOriginCheckForAnyClient` is derived from `hasBrowserOriginHeader`. So today, an **Origin-bearing non-UI / non-webchat client** is only origin-checked under that condition, not unconditionally.

This PR's gate is broader: any Origin-bearing request is checked pre-upgrade. The live proof below shows that a non-UI client sending an `Origin` not in `allowedOrigins` (case 5) and a trusted-proxy-forwarded origin (case 6) are **rejected**. That may change a configured Control UI policy into a broader gateway-client admission requirement for Origin-bearing non-UI clients.

**I am not unilaterally narrowing or broadening this.** Per the review, a gateway/security owner must decide:

> Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` become a pre-upgrade requirement for **every** Origin-bearing WebSocket client, or remain limited to the current browser/Control-UI/webchat policy scope?

- **Preserve client-aware scope (reviewer-recommended):** keep the existing post-handshake client-aware policy and only add a pre-upgrade gate if an equivalent safe browser-only discriminator is available pre-upgrade.
- **Approve broader origin enforcement:** a gateway/security owner intentionally applies the policy to all Origin-bearing clients, documents the compatibility change, and adds regression coverage for native/custom-scheme and proxy scenarios.

I'll adjust the gate to match the owner's decision. The code change itself is small and contained; the open question is the **enforcement boundary**, which code review cannot safely infer.

Likely owner per review routing: **eleqtrizit** (recent released work on gateway browser-origin enforcement).

## Evidence (current head `4f6e6ccadde`)

Live `verifyClient` execution against the production `createGatewayVerifyClient` at head `4f6e6ccadde` (redacted IPs in `203.0.113.x` / `10.0.0.x` documentation ranges; `127.0.0.1` loopback):

```
1. no Origin (CLI/native app)                         -> 101 ACCEPT
2. allowed Origin (Control UI allowlist)              -> 101 ACCEPT
3. disallowed Origin (cross-site browser)             -> 403 REJECT  origin not allowed
4. literal null Origin (opaque browser origin)        -> 403 REJECT  origin missing or invalid
5. non-UI client w/ Origin not in allowlist          -> 403 REJECT  origin not allowed
6. trusted-proxy forwarded (Origin not in allowlist)  -> 403 REJECT  origin not allowed
7. loopback local client, loopback Origin            -> 101 ACCEPT
```

Cases 5 and 6 are the compatibility-sensitive paths the review asked to document: a non-UI Origin-bearing client and a trusted-proxy-forwarded origin are both rejected by the current gate. Whether that rejection is desired is the scope decision above.

Unit tests: `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` (4/4 passing). No tokens, endpoints, or secrets; IPs are `127.0.0.1` / `203.0.113.x` / `10.0.0.x` documentation ranges.

## Scope

- `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, 57 lines) — `createGatewayVerifyClient`, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts:281`.
- `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` (new, 4 cases).
- `docs/gateway/security/websocket-origin-gate.md` (new) + link in `docs/gateway/security/index.md`.
- Reuses `checkBrowserOrigin` and `gateway.controlUi.*`. No forwarded-header, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, proxy-header, or `gateway.security.*` logic; no new settings.

target.title: fix(ui): restore first-run setup redirect after reconnect
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where first-time Control UI users could remain on an unconfigured chat screen after `openclaw.setup.detect` failed during a transient Gateway disconnect. The first-run redirect recorded the failed request as its only attempt, so a reconnect could not recover setup guidance.

A real-Gateway reproduction also exposed that Gateway hello canonicalizes the default session alias from `main` to `agent:<id>:main`. The old exact-URL guard treated that internal adoption as user navigation and suppressed the redirect even after a successful incomplete-setup result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Detection attempts are scoped to the Gateway client that owns them. Failed attempts become retryable, late results from obsolete clients cannot redirect the page, and a successful current-client result remains terminal across later reconnects.

The default-landing guard now resolves only the `session` query parameter through the existing Gateway session-default contract before comparison. Path, hash, other query parameters, and genuinely different sessions still have to match exactly.

## User Impact

Fresh users who lose the Gateway during the initial setup check are guided to Model Setup after reconnection without reloading the Control UI. Gateway canonicalization of the default chat session no longer blocks that guidance, while explicit session navigation still wins.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An interrupted first-run setup detection retries against a reconnected real Gateway and redirects after the successful incomplete-setup response.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node 24.15.0, Google Chrome, commit `c24e9a79ce17` (tree `e3e0589860b2`, matching the tested checkout).
- **Current-head refresh:** GitHub head `beb7be792770` (tree `98064f009736`) is rebased on upstream `52d49a69b2f`. The conflict resolution retains current `main` Custodian onboarding behavior, preserves the reconnect E2E scenario, and aligns its redirect assertion with the current `?firstRun=1` navigation contract. Exact-head GitHub CI passed, including `openclaw/ci-gate`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29640959950/job/88071729624.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** A one-shot `node --input-type=module` Playwright harness launched the source Vite Control UI and an isolated real `openclaw gateway run`, killed the Gateway immediately after the first browser `openclaw.setup.detect` frame, restarted the same isolated Gateway, and waited for the visible Model Setup route.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of the real `node` + Gateway + Chrome run (copied live stdout):

  ```text
  RESULT gateway_starts=2 browser_sockets=7 detect_requests=3 detect_responses=1 final_path=/settings/model-setup heading=1
  PASS real Gateway reconnect recovered first-run setup redirect
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The browser survived repeated reconnect attempts, retried setup detection until one response completed, changed to `/settings/model-setup`, and rendered the `Connect your AI` heading.
- **What was not tested:** The real Gateway used an isolated local state directory and explicit loopback `auth=none`; a credential-bearing remote Gateway was not used. The separate deterministic Chromium regression continues to use the repository Gateway WebSocket mock.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/model-setup/first-run.test.ts
```

The regressions cover failure followed by a replacement client, completion followed by a later replacement, canonical main-session adoption, explicit navigation to another session, one-request deduplication, and one-redirect behavior.

- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no persisted state or configuration changes.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - existing admin-scope and advertised-method gates are unchanged.

target.title: fix(canvas): classify deleteSurface and dataModelUpdate as v0.9-only actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` are A2UI v0.9 actions — only `surfaceUpdate` and `beginRendering` exist in v0.8. But the validator only checked for `createSurface` as a v0.9 indicator. Unversioned `deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` payloads were incorrectly classified as v0.8 and passed validation, then sent to the native client which cannot process them.

The native client's own schema confirms these are protocol-level action keys:
```js
// a2ui.bundle.js:4087
message: "A2UI Protocol message must have exactly one of: surfaceUpdate, dataModelUpdate, beginRendering, deleteSurface."
```

## Root Cause

`a2ui-jsonl.ts:88` — `if (explicitVersion === "v0.9" || actionKeys[0] === "createSurface")` — only `createSurface` triggered v0.9 detection. `deleteSurface` and `dataModelUpdate` fell through to `sawV08 = true`.

## Fix

target.title: fix(canvas): surface eval errors instead of silently swallowing them
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `canvas.eval` returns a non-string result or error from the node (e.g. `{ payload: { error: "SyntaxError: Unexpected token" } }`), the old code returned `jsonResult({ ok: true })` — a generic success signal. The agent sees success even when the JavaScript evaluation failed.

## Root Cause

The `raw` cast at `tool.ts:160-162` only recognized `{ payload?: { result?: string } }`. When `result` was absent or non-string (number, null, undefined), control fell through to `return jsonResult({ ok: true })`. Gateway errors in other payload shapes were silently discarded.

## Fix

- Type cast widened to `{ payload?: { result?: unknown; error?: string } }`
- Non-string results return `{ ok: false, error, result }` so error context is visible to the agent
- String results are unchanged (existing behavior preserved)

Files changed:
- `extensions/canvas/src/tool.ts`: Refactored `case "eval"` handler

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Non-string eval results and errors are now surfaced instead of silently swallowed
- Commands / artifacts:

  - `npx vitest run extensions/canvas/src/tool.test.ts` — 12 passed, 1 skipped (symlink on Windows)
- Observed result: All existing tests pass. Non-string results correctly return `{ ok: false, error, result }`.

target.title: fix(canvas): stop sending undefined coords on partial placement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent calls `canvas present` with only a subset of placement coordinates (e.g. only `width` and `height`), the old code constructed a placement object with `undefined` values for the missing fields. `JSON.stringify` silently strips `undefined` keys, so the node receives incomplete placement data.

## Root Cause

`readFiniteNumberParam` returns `undefined` for absent keys. The code at `tool.ts:122-140` unconditionally set all four fields then checked `Number.isFinite` on each to decide whether to include placement at all — but when some are finite and some aren't, the whole object (with undefined entries) is sent downstream.

## Fix

Only defined placement values are collected into the `placement` record. The gate check uses `Object.keys(placement).length > 0` instead of four individual `Number.isFinite` checks.

Files changed:
- `extensions/canvas/src/tool.ts`: Refactored `case "present"` placement construction

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Partial placement coords no longer send `undefined` to the node
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff main --check -- extensions/canvas/` — clean
  - `npx vitest run extensions/canvas/src/tool.test.ts` — 12 passed, 1 skipped (symlink on Windows)
- Observed result: All existing tests pass. Placement object now only contains defined coordinates, preventing silent `undefined` propagation through JSON serialization.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses. Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

This upgrades both hooks from fire-and-forget (void) to sequential modifying hooks. Replaces the closed #61485 with a clean implementation against current `main`.

- `llm_input` handlers can now return `{ block, blockReason, prompt, systemPrompt }` to block or modify the LLM call
- `llm_output` handlers can now return `{ assistantTexts }` to replace the model response (e.g. for redaction)
- Handlers returning `void` behave identically to before (fully backward compatible)

## User Impact

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override what's sent to the model
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the response (e.g. PII redaction)
- Existing plugins that return `void` are unaffected — fully backward compatible
- `allowPromptInjection=false` strips prompt/systemPrompt overrides but preserves block/blockReason

### Mutation semantics

**llm_input:**
- `prompt` / `systemPrompt`: first-setter-wins across priority-ordered handlers
- `block` / `blockReason`: sticky-true (any handler blocks; `shouldStop` exits early)
- Subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy — prompt fields stripped when `false`
- `evolveEvent` propagates the **accumulated merged result** to lower-priority handlers and resets `imagesCount` to 0
- `systemPrompt` override applied to active model session via `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt`

**llm_output:**
- `assistantTexts`: last-setter-wins with evolved event propagation
- Later hooks see prior modifications, preventing silent overwrites of higher-priority redactions

### Security boundaries

- `PluginBlockedError` sentinel skips failover/retry classification (not a transient provider failure)
- `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` strips `prompt`/`systemPrompt` from results when `allowPromptInjection=false`
- `historyMessages` deep-cloned via `cloneHookMessages` before passing to hooks
- `lastAssistant` deep-cloned via `structuredClone` before passing to `llm_output` hooks

### Cross-runner contract

- Embedded runner: fully consumes modifying results (block, prompt/systemPrompt override, output replacement)
- Harness helpers (`runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook`): upgraded from `void` to `Promise<Result | undefined>` so CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runners can consume modifying results
- Backward compatible — existing fire-and-forget callers discard the promise

### Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` | Add `PluginHookLlmInputResult`, `PluginHookLlmOutputResult` types with documented mutation semantics; add `llm_input` to prompt injection hook names; update handler map signatures |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | Add `evolveEvent` to `ModifyingHookPolicy`; wire into `runModifyingHook` using accumulated result; upgrade `runLlmInput`/`runLlmOutput` from `runVoidHook` to `runModifyingHook` |
| `src/plugins/registry.ts` | Add `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook`; handle `llm_input` in prompt injection guard |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Add `PluginBlockedError`; await `llm_input`/`llm_output` results; apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides to active session; wire output replacement |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Import `PluginBlockedError`; handle with `hook_block` error kind, skip failover |
| `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts` | Upgrade `runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook` to return `Promise<Result>` |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` | 18 unit tests: block, override, priority merge, A>B>C accumulated-result evolution, backward compat, error handling |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts` | 6 e2e tests: full plugin lifecycle from `api.on()` -> loader -> registry -> runner -> result |

## Evidence

### E2E plugin lifecycle proof (6 tests)

Exercises the full path from plugin `api.on()` registration through loader, registry, hook runner, to result consumption:

1. **Block**: Plugin returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "Content policy violation" }` when prompt contains "BLOCKED" — runner returns block result
2. **Prompt rewrite**: Plugin returns `{ prompt: "[SANITIZED] " + event.prompt }` — runner returns rewritten prompt
3. **System prompt override**: Plugin returns `{ systemPrompt: "compliance prompt" }` — runner returns override
4. **Output redaction**: Plugin replaces `secret` with `[REDACTED]` in `assistantTexts` via `llm_output` — runner returns redacted output
5. **Backward compat**: Plugin returns `void` from both hooks — runner returns `undefined` (no modification)
6. **allowPromptInjection=false**: Plugin returns block + prompt + systemPrompt — constraint strips prompt/systemPrompt, preserves block

### Unit tests (18 tests)

Cover hook merger internals: merge policy, evolveEvent, imagesCount reset, error handling, empty array suppression.

### Verification commands

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts  # 6/6 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts      # 18/18 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm.test.ts                # 5/5 pass (backward compat)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions                                          # typecheck clean
```

## ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed

All 3 findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103959#issuecomment-4939779091) fixed:

1. **evolveEvent uses accumulated result** — `hooks.ts`: `evolveEvent(event, result)` not `evolveEvent(event, handlerResult)`. A>B>C priority test validates.
2. **systemPrompt applied to active session** — `attempt.ts`: `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt()` called after hook override.
3. **Harness helpers return results** — `lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts`: both return `Promise<Result | undefined>` for cross-runner consumption.

## Supersedes

Replaces #61485 (closed by maintainer as stale)

target.title: fix(qqbot): send quoted media paths with spaces
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot outbound media tags did not recognize quoted self-closing media paths containing spaces, such as `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />`.

`normalizeMediaTags()` accepted whitespace-free `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values, but the same parser stopped matching when the quoted attribute value contained a common local filename with a space. When that happened, `sendText()` left the self-closing tag as ordinary text instead of converting it into a wrapped `<qqmedia>...</qqmedia>` block for the media sender.

The narrow pre-fix trigger was:

```text
<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
```

Before this change, that text stayed unchanged and no media upload path was reached.

## Why This Change Was Made

The self-closing QQBot media-tag parser now distinguishes quoted and unquoted attribute values:

- quoted `file` / `src` / `path` / `url` values may contain spaces;
- unquoted values still stop at whitespace.

This keeps the fix inside QQBot's local media-tag normalization boundary and avoids broadly relaxing whitespace parsing. Existing wrapped tags, whitespace-free unquoted self-closing tags, alias resolution, sandbox/root checks, media kind routing, and outbound sender behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

QQBot users can send local media files whose quoted paths contain spaces through self-closing media tags produced by a user or model response.

For example, a reply containing `<qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />` now enters the existing QQBot media upload path instead of being delivered as literal text.

## Evidence

Focused parser proof:

```text
input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file='C:/tmp/foo bar.png' />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia alt="upload proof" file="C:/tmp/foo bar.png" />
output: <qqmedia>C:/tmp/foo bar.png</qqmedia>

input:  <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
output: <qqmedia file=C:/tmp/foo bar.png />
```

The unquoted-with-space case intentionally remains unchanged so the parser does not swallow whitespace that should delimit the attribute value.

User-realistic outbound path covered by test:

```text
user/model QQBot reply text
  -> <qqmedia file=".../tagged report.docx" />
  -> sendText()
  -> normalizeMediaTags()
  -> <qqmedia>.../tagged report.docx</qqmedia>
  -> media tag dispatch
  -> sendMedia()
```

The outbound regression creates a temporary file named `tagged report.docx`, sends it through `sendText()` as a quoted self-closing `<qqmedia file="..." />` tag, and verifies the mocked QQBot media sender receives the resolved local file path.

Live QQBot behavior proof:

```text

  -> QQBot WebSocket connected
  -> real C2C user sent "proof"
```

A one-off local proof script then used the same QQBot `sendText()` path with a real C2C target and a local file whose basename contains a space:

target.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration
target.body:
Related to #110186

## What Problem This Solves

The STRICT migration introduced in v2026.7.2 crashes the gateway on startup when legacy non-STRICT SQLite tables contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (or TEXT values in BLOB columns). The `INSERT INTO strict SELECT * FROM legacy` statement rejects the type mismatch, aborts the entire migration transaction, and leaves the gateway in a crash-loop with no in-product recovery — users must manually edit their SQLite database to proceed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `node:sqlite` driver writes `Buffer.from()` JavaScript values as SQLite BLOB type. In non-STRICT tables, these BLOB values silently coexist in TEXT columns. When PR #108663 (`30ae21fca7`) introduced STRICT migration, it used a bare `INSERT INTO strict SELECT col1, col2 FROM legacy` that passes values through without type normalization. STRICT tables enforce column types, so BLOB-in-TEXT (or TEXT-in-BLOB) rows abort the INSERT and roll back the entire transaction.

Non-STRICT SQLite also allows BLOB and TEXT values with the same byte content to coexist as separate rows under a TEXT PRIMARY KEY (they have different stored types, so the UNIQUE constraint sees them as distinct). After CAST, these would collide. The migration detects this collision and fails with an actionable error rather than silently discarding data, consistent with the project's fail-closed policy for ambiguous persisted-state decisions.

Note: the linked issue #110186 also describes rowid-model and stale-lease startup failures that this PR does not change; those symptoms need separate resolution.

## User Impact

- Users upgrading from v2026.7.1 to v2026.7.2 whose databases contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (e.g., `config_health_entries.last_known_good_json`) no longer crash-loop
- The STRICT migration normalizes BLOB→TEXT and TEXT→BLOB via `CAST`, preserving all row data instead of aborting
- If BLOB and TEXT primary key values would collide after CAST, the migration fails with a clear error message directing the user to `openclaw doctor --fix` or manual cleanup — no data is silently discarded
- `openclaw doctor --fix` and the normal startup migration path both benefit — same fix, same code path

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.18.0 (SQLite bundled), branch `fix/strict-blob-text-cast-110186`, SHA `ae8a1a2a40

### Real v2026.7.1→current upgrade through repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema (current head)

Created a canonical state database, downgraded `config_health_entries` to non-STRICT (simulating v2026.7.1), inserted a BLOB-in-TEXT row via `Buffer.from('{"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}')`, then ran `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema`:

```console
=== Pre-downgrade (STRICT) ===
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.json vtype=null
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json vtype=text

BLOB row: {"config_path":"/home/user/.openclaw/credentials/ai.json","vtype":"blob"}

=== Running repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema (doctor) ===
Result: {
  "changes": [
    "Migrated shared state session watch cursors → provenance column (0 ambient, 0 sentinels removed)",
    "Migrated shared state tables to SQLite STRICT typing (1)"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}
```

target.title: fix(zalo): trigger cleanup when abort signal already fired
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a shutdown race in the Zalo channel provider. When the gateway stop `AbortSignal` was already aborted before `monitorZaloProvider` registered its listener, the abort event was not replayed and startup continued into polling or webhook resource acquisition.

## Why This Change Was Made

The monitor now checks `abortSignal.aborted` immediately before listener registration and before acquiring hosted-media routes, registering a webhook, or starting polling. The normal later-abort path remains unchanged.

The fix stays inside the Zalo plugin and adds no config, protocol, SDK, dependency, or compatibility surface.

## User Impact

Fast gateway stops and overlapping account lifecycle transitions no longer allow Zalo polling, webhook mutation, or local HTTP-route startup after shutdown has already won the race.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The committed integration test exercises the complete production boundary:

`configured OpenClaw Zalo account` -> `zaloPlugin.gateway.startAccount` -> `startZaloGatewayAccount` -> real account probe -> `monitorZaloProvider`

It does not mock the Zalo API module, monitor, gateway runtime, config resolver, `fetch`, `AbortSignal`, or plugin HTTP-route registry. The production Zalo HTTP client connects over a real loopback TCP socket using its supported `ZALO_API_URL` override. The loopback endpoint returns normal Zalo-shaped responses and records every API method observed without exposing the configured token.

The same test was run against the PR base and the reviewed head:

| Revision | Result | API methods observed after configured gateway startup | Local routes after return |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base `db3213264a` | 0 passed, 2 failed | polling: `getMe`, `getWebhookInfo`; webhook: `getMe`, `setWebhook`, `deleteWebhook` | 0 |
| Head `14a96a5713` | 2 passed, 0 failed | polling: `getMe`; webhook: `getMe` | 0 |

`getMe` is the production gateway's account probe. On the fixed head, the already-aborted monitor performs no polling inspection, update polling, webhook registration/deletion, or local route registration after that probe.

Base failure excerpts:

```text
polling: expected [ 'getMe', 'getWebhookInfo' ] to deeply equal [ 'getMe' ]
webhook: expected [ 'getMe', 'setWebhook', 'deleteWebhook' ] to deeply equal [ 'getMe' ]
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       2 failed (2)
```

Head result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       2 passed (2)
```

Focused related validation on the final head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/zalo/src/channel.pre-aborted.integration.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts \
  extensions/zalo/src/channel.startup.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       10 passed (10)
```

Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass. The standard pushed-head CI remains authoritative for full build, lint, and test-type gates.

Proof boundary: this is a real-process, real-socket integration against a deterministic loopback Zalo API endpoint, not a claim of testing the public Zalo service. That substitution is appropriate for this race because the asserted behavior is the absence and ordering of API/resource acquisition after a pre-aborted lifecycle; the test fails on the base by observing the exact unwanted production HTTP methods and passes on the fixed head with only the required account probe.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound check-workflows subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local workflow sanity checks could hang indefinitely when an external linter, Go fallback, or pre-commit bootstrap command stopped making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/check-workflows.mjs` now applies a bounded timeout to each subprocess it launches, escalates non-cooperative children after a short grace period, and reports which command timed out. POSIX subprocesses are terminated through their process group; Windows timeout escalation uses `taskkill /T /F` so descendants launched by wrappers are included. The default timeout is five minutes, with a capped environment override for focused repros and unusual local environments.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear failure instead of a stuck workflow sanity check when a dependency command hangs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- scripts/check-workflows.mjs scripts/check-workflows.d.mts test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/check-workflows.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-script-declarations.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused Windows coverage in `test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts` verifies timeout escalation uses `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` after the SIGTERM grace period.
- Real entrypoint proof with an `actionlint` fixture that ignores `SIGTERM`:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM
status: 1
stderr: [check-workflows] timed out after 500ms: actionlint .github/workflows/android-release.yml ... .github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml
```

<details>
<summary>proof-check-workflows-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "--version") process.exit(0);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});
setInterval(() => {}, 10_000);
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint"

set +e
PATH="$proof_dir/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 "$node_bin" scripts/check-workflows.mjs >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs\n'
printf 'fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>
